[Benzinga news, 2026-10-26T10:31:56Z, by staff] Bristol Myers Squibb and SystImmune Announce Positive Phase 3 Results for Izalontamab Brengitecan in NSCLC
Bristol Myers Squibb and partner SystImmune reported positive interim results from the Phase 3 PANKU-Lung01 study, showing that the drug candidate izalontamab brengitecan (Iza-Bren) doubled median progression-free survival in patients with previously-treated EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
Bristol Myers Squibb and SystImmune, a subsidiary of Sichuan Biokin Pharmaceutical, announced positive interim analysis results from the Phase 3 PANKU-Lung01 clinical trial. The study evaluated izalontamab brengitecan (Iza-Bren), an EGFRxHER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate, in patients with previously-treated EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Results indicated that the treatment doubled median progression-free survival compared to chemotherapy. Bristol Myers Squibb management highlighted the findings as an important inflection point for the asset, noting its potential to address significant unmet needs across multiple tumor types. The company is currently advancing the development of Iza-Bren as part of its oncology portfolio.

memos_so_far.headline: BMY and SystImmune: Iza-Bren met its primary endpoint at a Phase 3 interim in EGFR-mutated lung cancer, median PFS 11.1 vs 5.7 months
reasoning: Source: the companies' joint press release (relayed via Barchart; Benzinga 03:54 ET and 06:31 ET). Quoted: 'Iza-Bren Hits Primary Endpoint In Phase 3 PANKU-Lung01 Interim Analysis, Median PFS 11.1 Versus 5.7 Months (HR 0.40) Over Platinum Chemotherapy In EGFR-Mutated NSCLC'.

What changed: the first Phase 3 readout for an EGFRxHER3 antibody-drug conjugate that BMY licensed from SystImmune, a Sichuan Biokin subsidiary. It now has a registrational result in previously treated EGFR-mutated NSCLC.
Timing: published before the open, no session has traded it. A separate item on 10/25 (BioNTech/BMY pumitamig Phase 2) is a different drug.
Pre-market: no IEX prints for BMY yet against the 61.49 close.

memos_so_far.headline: Good data, small lever: one partnered asset in one second-line indication barely moves a $125B company
reasoning: What changed: Iza-Bren now has Phase 3 support in previously treated EGFR-mutated NSCLC. HR 0.40 for progression-free survival is strong, but the comparison is against platinum chemotherapy, the weakest standard arm in this setting.

Size: BMY's market cap is about $125B. BMY shares the asset with SystImmune: it has ex-China rights, and the profit split is not stated in the release. Peak sales in this one line of therapy are a fraction of BMY's revenue base, which is about $48B a year. For BMY to reprice by 5% or more, the market must have assigned near-zero odds to Iza-Bren. Sichuan Biokin's earlier China data made success the expected case.
The crew's own record points the same way: conference and interim readouts on large caps have rarely moved the stock in the cases on file (ESMO pattern).
Would prove this wrong: BMY up more than 4% at today's close with no other news. That would mean the market had priced Iza-Bren much lower than I assume.
objections: No mispricing large enough to clear costs on a 10-day horizon; likely a 1-2% move that the open will price.
